newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam nudges dong rate lower, dollar in demand.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam nudges dong rate lower, dollar in demand.

text.p: The State Bank of Vietnam has nudged its official rate for the dong against the dollar slightly lower, giving the local currency room to move down a few ticks in the interbank market, a central bank official said on Monday.
The official, who declined to be identified, said the rate was pegged at 11,034 per dollar last Friday compared with 11,030 previously, and then moved again on Saturday to 11,036.
Commercial banks may buy and sell at rates up to one percent on either side of the official rate.
The new band, based on a pivot rate of 11,036 per dollar, has 10,926 as an upper dong limit and 11,146 as a lower limit.
State-owned Vietcombank quoted a rate of 11,102/13 per dollar on Monday morning, but two foreign banks in Hanoi were quoting rates of 11,136/46 and 11,129/40.

"Looking at the situation in the forex market, we decided to adjust a bit. The buying and selling rates set by the commercial banks have been moving up a bit," the central bank official said, referring to rising interbank quotes for the number of dong per dollar.

The cental bank, which commercial bankers say is seeking a very gradual depreciation of the dong, last month widened the official fluctuation band to one percent on either side of its pivot rate from 0.5 percent.
But, with corporate demand for dollars strong, the dong had moved to the bottom of its new, wider band by the end of last week and market liquidity had begun to dry up.
With the dong now on, or very close to, its lower limit again, business remains very thin.
"There's still strong demand around for dollars. There's small amounts going through. But it's nowhere near as liquid as it should or could be," said one treasury expert.

He said current demand for the U.S. currency presented the authorities with an opportunity to implement its policy of gradual depreciation, and predicted that the central bank would continue to peg its official dong-per-dollar rate higher.
However, the central bank official indicated there would be no dramatic moves.
"We want the rate not to move too fast and we want the exchange rate stable. That is the goal of the State Bank of Vietnam," he said.
